run1.title: Baseline
run1.lesson: Left to itself, gradient descent finds a slow fade instead of a reset, and a write gate that records time rather than distance. Both work a little at 10 seconds and not at all at 20. The memory was in F, but leaky.

run2.title: Erase penalty times ten
run2.lesson: Charging more for erasing away from food did not push the gate toward food; it shut the gate everywhere. With no erase at all, the tallies filled to the ceiling within a trip and the brain could not home. A scalar gate cannot be penalised into firing on five ticks out of three hundred.

run3.title: Two seconds at food
run3.lesson: Four times more food ticks did not teach the reset either, but it rebalanced the whole trip: a lower write gate, tallies off the ceiling, and, for the first time, a write gate that follows speed (+0.94). First brain to home on 20-second trips. Memory in F by a wide margin: 1.99 with it, 4.75 without.

run4.title: Five trips per episode
run4.lesson: More trips in a row did not make the erase gate fire at food (0.0045 at food, 0.0085 away: it erases LESS at food than elsewhere). The fade simply absorbed the dirty board, and the extra trips only cost score: 2.30 at 20 s against run 3's 1.90. Prediction failed. It did give the first 30-second numbers: 2.37 with F, 5.80 without, on trips it never trained at, so the memory generalises to longer wanders.

run5.title: Erase penalty ×10, warm start
run5.lesson: The penalty did nothing to the erase gate, because at 0.5 times a gate of 0.01 it adds 0.005 to a loss of about 2: a rounding error. Run 2 had died for cold-start reasons, not because the penalty was strong. What run 5 did show is the danger of long training near the ceiling: after a good stretch (best frozen exam 1.41 at iteration 400) it collapsed twice, and the second time it did not recover; the final network is worse than a random walk. Its best checkpoint ties run 4 at 30 s (2.37). Lesson: the optimiser needs a schedule that shrinks its steps late in a run.

run6.title: Stretch to 30 s, with cosine decay
run6.lesson: Trained at 30 seconds for the first time. By iteration 400 its frozen exam at 30 s was 1.77, far under the untrained 2.37, with the memory in F (5.48 without). Then the familiar collapse at 500 (write gate 0.38 to 0.64, loss to 12) and it did not recover by 600, so it was killed. Cosine decay alone was not enough: at iteration 500 of 1,200 the rate was still two thirds of full. Restarted as run 6B from the 1.77 checkpoint at a third of the base rate. Note: this stage was started on run 5's 64-trip frozen exam of 1.41, not on the running-score rule (which no run had met); see the narrative.

run6B.title: Run 6 restarted at a third of the learning rate
run6B.lesson: No collapse in 800 iterations at 30 seconds. Final network: 2.13 at 30 s with F, 5.91 without (22% arrived); 1.85 at 20 s. The lower rate is the fix for the late collapses: from here every warm start trains at 3e-4. The score has plateaued around 2.1 at 30 s, well above the 0.75 floor. Still a fade (0.005 at food, 0.009 away), write~speed +0.53, tallies saturated a third of the time at 30 s: the three things that still separate it from the fly.

run7.title: Erase penalty 20, warm
run7.lesson: Even a real penalty barely moved the gate: away-from-food erase went 0.0081 to 0.0075 in 200 iterations, and at-food erase fell rather than rose. The diagnosis is structural. The erase gate is a sigmoid whose bias sits near -5, where the curve is almost flat: its slope there is about 0.007, so every gradient reaching the gate, penalty or benefit, is multiplied by 0.007 before it can move anything. The gate is not refusing to learn the reset; it cannot hear the signal. Killed at 200; the fix is tested as run 7B.

run7B.title: Erase gate given a voice (bias +2.5)
run7B.lesson: The first run in which the erase gate prefers food. On the 200-trip test it erases 0.027 per tick at food against 0.009 away, a ratio of 3, with peaks of 0.06 at food; every earlier run was at or below 1. The ratio grew through training (1.1 at iteration 200, 1.5 at 700). It is a leaning, not yet a reset: the fly-like target is near 1 at food and near 0 away. The strong starting fade cost score, 2.55 at 30 s against the parent's 2.13, and 800 iterations were not enough to recover it. Prediction partly met: away-from-food erase did fall below 0.01; at-food erase reached 0.027 mean, short of 0.05; score did not recover.

run8.title: Run 7B continued, unchanged
run8.lesson: Continuing the line with nothing changed did not sharpen the food preference. Over 300 iterations the erase ratio on the sample trip sat between 1.3 and 1.6, with peaks at food of 0.07 to 0.10, while the score recovered to about 2.2. The gate can move now, but with this signal it settles on a mild preference for food rather than a clean reset. Killed at 300 to spend the time on a stronger push.

run8B.title: Food stand 4 s with an audible gate
run8B.lesson: Doubling the food ticks did not sharpen the reset: on the 200-trip test the erase ratio is 3.0 (food 0.027, away 0.009), no better than run 7B's 3, with peaks at food of 0.06. The score held rather than improved: 2.28 at 30 s on the standard exam, though its frozen checks on other trips reached 1.76. Prediction failed on the ratio, met on the score holding. Lesson: once the gate can hear, more food ticks are not the missing signal; the preference for food is real but small, and nothing on the warm-start line has pushed it past a ratio of about 3.

run9.title: Cold start, audible gate, penalty 20
run9.lesson: From scratch, the penalty of 20 did what it did in run 2: it drove the erase gate shut within 200 iterations (0.0001 per tick away from food, 0.001 at food), which puts the sigmoid back on its flat part, deaf again, before any memory had formed. No F-versus-no-F gap by iteration 300. Killed under the five-minute rule. Lesson: on a cold start the penalty must be small enough that the gate stays audible while the memory is being built; 20 is a warm-start number.

run9B.title: Cold start, audible gate, penalty 2
run9B.lesson: Killed at 500 by its own prediction: no memory gap formed (F 2.42, no-F 2.42). The gate closed to 0.001 per tick by iteration 200 even at a penalty of 2, because before any memory exists erasing has no benefit and every gradient says erase less. Worse, the strong early fade (0.07 per tick at the start) wiped the tallies during the phase when the memory had to form; run 3, same seed and a deaf gate, had a 0.5 gap by iteration 300. Lesson: an audible erase gate helps a network that already has a memory (run 7B) and hurts one that does not. The reset can only be learned second, after the tally.

run10.title: Second bias shift, the ratchet test
run10.lesson: The ratio did ratchet, once measured properly. On the single training-check trip it looked stuck near 1.8, but on the 200-trip test the erase gate fires 0.075 per tick at food against 0.010 away: a ratio of 7.4, up from 3 in runs 7B and 8B, with peaks of 0.20 on the test trip and 0.2 to 0.3 during training. The gate is learning a spike at food, one tick at a time. It is also the best earned 30-second score of the night: 2.10 on the standard exam, 23% arriving, with frozen checks under 1.5. Prediction met on the ratio (above 5) and on the score; at-food erase 0.075 is above the 0.05 target. Still not a full reset (that would be near 1 at food), but the clearest one yet.

run11.title: Seed 1 replication of run 3
run11.lesson: The 10-second learning replicated from a different random start, and faster: promoted at iteration 619 against run 3's 804, with a frozen gap of 0.9 (1.46 with F, 2.40 without). The transfer to 20 seconds did not: 400 iterations after promotion the gap had not opened, and the driver's stop rule ended the run. The write gate sat near 0.7 with write strength 0.10, the run 1 pattern where the tallies saturate on longer trips. So the compass-and-tally recipe is robust to the seed; how quickly a given seed adapts to longer trips is not. Queued as 11B: the same network continued at 20 s with the gap rule suspended, since run 3 also needed time after its promotion.

run12.title: Third bias shift
run12.lesson: The ratchet held a third time. On the 200-trip test the erase gate fires 0.213 per tick at food against 0.010 away, a ratio of 20, with peaks of 0.50 on the test trip and 0.57 to 0.67 during training. The reset is now a spike that opens more than halfway at food and nowhere else. The score held: 2.21 at 30 s on the standard exam, 24% arriving, against 2.10 for run 10. Prediction met: ratio target 12, at-food target 0.15.

run13.title: Slow-half fast-half world
run13.lesson: Trained on a world where time and distance disagree, then tested on the standard world: 1.98 at 30 s on the final checkpoint and 1.91 at its best, the lowest earned 30-second scores of the night, with 25% arriving. Write-versus-speed on the standard exam is +0.69 (+0.67 at the best checkpoint), up from run 10's +0.67 but short of the 0.9 predicted. The harder training world made a better brain for the easy one: forcing distance-weighting during training improved homing where speed merely drifts. The reset survived the change of world (ratio 7).

run11B.title: Seed 1, continued at 20 s
run11B.lesson: Given 800 more iterations with the gap rule suspended, seed 1 did begin to transfer: the frozen gap opened from zero to about 0.8 and the running score fell from 4.4 to 3.7. But on the 200-trip test at 20 s it scores 3.87 with F against 4.61 without, still worse than the random walk's 3.61, with 26 compass cells and tallies saturated 59% of the time (write strength 0.165, twice seed 0's). Verdict: the recipe's 10-second stage replicates across seeds; its 20-second transfer is much slower for seed 1 and was not complete after 1,200 iterations. The robustness claim is narrowed to: compass cells and a working tally emerge from any seed; how fast the tally adapts to longer trips depends on the seed.

run14.title: Fourth bias shift
run14.lesson: The ratchet keeps working: on the 200-trip test the erase gate fires 0.37 per tick at food against 0.011 away, a ratio of 33, with peaks of 0.78 on the test trip and 0.83 to 0.91 during training. Away from food it has never moved from about 0.01. The score is 2.06 at 30 s, 26% arriving, the best of the ratchet line and within noise of the campaign best. Ratios across the shifts: 3, 7, 20, 33. Prediction partly met: at-food target 0.4, peaks target 0.8.

run15.title: Delta rule, cold start (Peter's proposal)
run15.lesson: Stopped by the gap rule at iteration 800: no memory formed at all. Under the delta rule F writes only what it failed to predict, so F converged on predicting the network's own next activity from its last, and once it did that it stopped writing; the tallies never accumulated steps, and the write strength and A did not move from their starting values after iteration 100 (0.108 and 0.082, flat). Peter's prediction, that delta would keep a wider memory gap and free the erase gate, did not hold in this form. Two honest caveats: this was a cold start with the deaf-gate recipe, and a warm start from a Hebb-trained network, or a delta rule applied only on the columns A selects, might behave differently. As run, the delta rule is a predictor, not a tally.

run16.title: Fifth bias shift
run16.lesson: Five shifts: on the 200-trip test the erase gate averages 0.52 per tick across the food stand and reaches 0.93 at its peak, against 0.010 away from food, a ratio of 53. During training the peaks were 0.95 to 0.98. The reset is now a wipe: the board is cleared at food and untouched elsewhere. Score 2.14 at 30 s, 25% arriving, within noise of runs 10, 12 and 14, so five rounds of the same move took the mean at food from 0.03 to 0.52 and the peak from 0.06 to 1 without costing the memory or the score. Ratios across the shifts: 3, 7, 20, 33, 53.

run17.title: Low-rate polish of the best line
run17.lesson: Small steps from run 13's best checkpoint on the standard world: 1.89 at 30 s on the final network and 1.81 at its best checkpoint, with 25% arriving and the memory in F (5.91 without). That is the lowest earned 30-second score of the night, about 2.4 times the hand brain's 0.75 floor. Frozen checks during training reached 1.28. The reset it inherited from run 10 is a mild one (ratio 9), since this line branched before the ratchet; the score line and the reset line are separate networks. Prediction met: target was at or under 1.85.

run18.title: Delta rule, warm from run 14
run18.lesson: Switching a working Hebb-trained tally to the delta rule destroyed the memory at once: no gap at 100, 200 or 300, score at or above a random walk. Killed at 300 by its own prediction. Both forms of the delta rule, cold and warm, fail to hold a tally, because a rule that writes only what F cannot predict stops writing exactly when the tally needs to keep adding. Negative result, in both forms; Peter's note gets a clear answer.

run19.title: The wiped network on the legs world
run19.lesson: The two ingredients stack. Trained on the slow-half fast-half world from run 14, then tested on the standard world: 1.62 at 30 s and 1.63 at 20 s, 33% arriving, the lowest earned scores of the campaign, with the memory in F (5.93 without). The reset survived the change of world: erase at food 0.38 against 0.008 away (ratio 49, peak 0.77). Write-versus-speed is +0.69. Prediction met on score (under 2.0) and reset (intact); write-versus-speed at +0.69 fell short of the 0.8 predicted. This is the best network of the night by every measure at once.

run20.title: The rival: fast weights disabled
run20.lesson: With A frozen at zero, the same 64-neuron network trained with run 3's exact recipe never learned to home at 10 seconds: running score between 2.35 and 2.43 for a thousand iterations, the random level, where the fast-weight version was at 1.96 by iteration 300 and promoted by 804. It hit the stage cap without earning it and was stopped rather than moved to 20 seconds. This is the level 4 comparison the plan was built for, and it came out one-sided: on this task and with this training, an activity-only memory did not form at all. Caveat, stated plainly: one recipe and one seed; an activity integrator might be trainable with a different learning rate, more neurons or more iterations. What the result does show is that the fast-weight version is far easier to train into a homing memory than the activity-only version, from the same start.

run22.title: 128 neurons, cold start
run22.lesson: Twice the neurons learned the 10-second stage in far fewer iterations: promoted at 302 against run 3's 804, and its best 10 s checkpoint scores 1.98 with F against 2.86 without, with 63 of 128 cells tuned to heading. But in 400 iterations at 20 seconds the memory gap never opened (4.02 with F, 4.06 without at iteration 700), the same stall seed 1 showed in run 11. Killed at 700 to give the CPU to run 23. Measured: capacity speeds up the first stage. Not settled: whether it would transfer with more iterations (run 11B eventually did, slowly). Caveat: this is a cold start with run 3's recipe; a 128-neuron warm start is not possible from a 64-neuron parent.

run21.title: Lid ±1 → ±2
run21.lesson: Negative, and informative. The lid did its job: cells pinned at the lid at 25 s fell from 43% (run 19) to 7.6%. But the decoded count barely improved (error 1.04 to 0.92 units at 25 s; 25% to 22% of the distance at the turn), and the score got worse: 1.96 at 30 s on the final network, 1.83 at its best checkpoint, against run 19's 1.62, with the return heading error rising from 55° to 66°. So saturation was not the main source of the count's error. The error grows in proportion to distance walked whether or not cells are pinned, which points at how the count is written (the write gate tracks speed at +0.69, not 1.0) and read, not at the ceiling. Measured throughout. The warm start also had to re-tune every readout to a doubled scale, which cost it the steering that run 19 had; a cold start with lid 2 might not pay that cost, but the count result says it would not gain much either.

run23.title: Train on 45-second wanders
run23.lesson: Negative on both lengths. Warm from run 19, 600 iterations at 45 s: 2.05 at 30 s (run 19: 1.62) and 2.51 at 45 s (run 19, never trained there: 2.15). The memory stayed in F (5.92 without F at 30 s) and the compass cells held at 32, but the reset weakened, erase at food falling from 0.38 to 0.18, and the running score on the training world never came under 3.2. Measured. Best guess for why: on 45-second trips the loss is noisier and the gradients from the last ten seconds of a 90-second return are a weak signal for what happened in the first 45, so each step moved the network less usefully than a 30-second step does; and the weaker reset suggests the longer trips shifted the balance toward fading. Longer training trips did not teach a better count; they taught a worse one, in this budget.

run24.title: Batch 32 → 64
run24.lesson: No effect on the exam: 1.62 at 30 s, the same as run 19, and 1.76 at 20 s against 1.63. On the training world its running score was the best of any run (2.47 against run 19's 2.73), so the steadier gradient did help the network fit the world it trains on, but the gain did not carry to the exam world. Measured. Best guess: the two-speed training world and the steady-speed exam world differ enough that fitting the first more tightly stops paying on the second, which is the same signal as run 21: the recipe is at a plateau that better optimisation alone does not move.

run25.title: Erase penalty 20 → 5
run25.lesson: Negative: 1.92 at 30 s (1.84 at the best checkpoint) against run 19's 1.62. The gate's behaviour barely changed: erase away from food 0.0077 to 0.0071 per tick (no rise), erase at food 0.38 to 0.31 (a slightly weaker reset), write follows speed +0.69 to +0.75, compass cells 32 to 31. Measured. The mechanism is not clear: the fade did not grow, so the cheaper penalty did not open the gate between food visits as the prediction feared. Either the slightly weaker wipe at food costs 0.3 of score, which seems large, or a run from this warm start varies by that much with the training dice. Run 27 reseeds run 19's own recipe to measure exactly that, and this verdict should be read after it.

run28.title: A charge on the size of F
run28.lesson: No effect on the exam: 1.60 at 30 s against run 19's 1.62, 1.72 at 20 s against 1.63, memory in F (5.95 without). The charge did what a charge does: write strength fell from 0.074 to 0.070 and the wipe at food rose from 0.38 to 0.51, so the board is kept smaller. The count was not written more finely in any way the exam could see (write follows speed +0.62 against +0.69). Measured. The 'smaller steps' lever, at this size, changes the board's housekeeping, not its accuracy.

run29.title: Many-speeds training world
run29.lesson: The knob did what it was meant to do to the gate and not to the score: write follows speed rose from +0.69 to +0.77 (+0.79 at the best checkpoint), the reset held (0.35 at food, 0.006 away), and the exam gave 1.67 at 30 s against 1.62, within noise. Measured. A world with many speed levels made the write gate a better speedometer; a better speedometer did not make a better homing score. So the count's remaining error is not mainly the speed weighting either. Six singles from run 19 now sit between 1.60 and 2.05, and the recipe's plateau at about 1.6 is real.

run31.title: Batch 64 plus a low-rate finish
run31.lesson: No effect: 1.64 at 30 s (1.67 at the best checkpoint) against 1.62, memory in F (5.94 without), compass cells 32, write follows speed +0.74. Its frozen checks during training reached 2.05, the best of the campaign, and again that did not carry to the exam. Measured. Two optimisation improvements stacked on the same network produced the same exam score as either alone or neither. The plateau at 1.6 is not optimisation noise.

run26.title: Polish of run 19 at 3e-5
run26.lesson: No gain: 1.71 at 30 s (1.66 at the best checkpoint) against 1.62. The move that gave run 17 a tenth of a point did not repeat on run 19. Measured. Together with runs 24 and 31 this settles that optimisation is not what holds the score at 1.6.

run27.title: Run 19's recipe, training dice reseeded
run27.lesson: The control that reframes the night. Same starting weights (run 14), same world, same knobs, only the seed for the training worlds changed: 1.99 at 30 s against run 19's 1.62, with the memory in F (5.90 without), the reset intact (0.31 at food, 0.009 away), 31 compass cells, write follows speed +0.57. Measured. So the recipe's seed-to-seed spread is at least 0.37 on a single run, and run 19's 1.62 was a fortunate draw as much as a better network. Every single-run comparison tonight (1.60 to 2.05) sits inside that spread, and so do several from the first night. From here on, a claim of improvement needs several seeds and a mean.

run32.title: Cold start on the many-speeds world
run32.lesson: Stopped at iteration 1900 with the 20-second stage stalled: promoted by the cap at 1000 with a 10 s memory (exam at 10 s: 1.51 with F, 2.61 without), then 900 iterations at 20 s with the gap opening and closing and never a running score under 4.7 (exam at 20 s: 3.43 with F, 4.11 without). Measured. A third cold start (after seed 1 and 128 neurons) that learns the short stage and stalls at the long one; run 3's clean transfer at iteration 804 looks like the exception, not the rule. The lineage question (does a network raised on the many-speeds world measure distance better?) stays open; it could not be reached in the budget.

run33.title: Erase bias shifted down by 2: a slower fade
run33.lesson: Killed at 300. The shift did lower the between-food fade as intended, from 0.008 to 0.0012 per tick at iteration 200, but it took the wipe at food down with it (0.38 to 0.06, peak 0.33), and the readout did not re-match to the slower fade: frozen checks went 6.06, 4.51, 6.37 and the running score was 5.87 at 300, worse than at 200. Measured. The fade and the readout are co-adapted, and moving the fade by hand broke both. Together with the exam-time fade test (less fade makes run 19 worse) this says the network's memory is a leaky integrator with its time constant and its readout learned as a pair; to get a longer-lasting count, both would have to be learned together from a start that does not first have to unlearn the short one. A cold start with a low erase floor would be the test, and it is not reachable tonight.

run30.title: Polish of run 29 on the many-speeds world
run30.lesson: No gain: 1.78 at 30 s against run 29's 1.67 and run 19's 1.62, all inside the recipe's seed spread. Measured. The last of the optimisation-side runs; none of them moved the exam.

run34.title: Run 19's recipe, seed 2
run34.lesson: 1.61 at 30 s (1.53 at 20 s), memory in F, reset 0.32 at food and 0.009 away, write follows speed +0.64, 34 compass cells. One of five draws of the same recipe: 1.62, 1.99, 1.61, 1.66, 1.73, mean 1.72, spread about 0.15 with one bad draw. Measured.

run35.title: Run 19's recipe, seed 3
run35.lesson: 1.66 at 30 s (1.55 at 20 s), memory in F, reset 0.313 at food and 0.0079 away, write follows speed +0.72, 29 compass cells. One of five draws of the same recipe: 1.62, 1.99, 1.61, 1.66, 1.73, mean 1.72, spread about 0.15 with one bad draw. Measured.

run36.title: Run 19's recipe, seed 4
run36.lesson: 1.73 at 30 s (1.78 at 20 s), memory in F, reset 0.2 at food and 0.0063 away, write follows speed +0.72, 30 compass cells. One of five draws of the same recipe: 1.62, 1.99, 1.61, 1.66, 1.73, mean 1.72, spread about 0.15 with one bad draw. Measured.

run37.title: Cold start with a low erase floor
run37.lesson: Learned the 10-second stage and earned promotion at iteration 804 (exam at 10 s: 1.81 with F, 2.72 without), then stalled at 20 seconds and was stopped at 1500 (exam at 20 s: 4.19 with F, 4.28 without). The striking measurement is the fade itself: it started at 0.0009 per tick and training raised it to 0.014 by the end of the 10-second stage, above the 0.008 of the warm-start lineage. Given a slow-fading count from the start, gradient descent chose a faster fade. Measured. With the exam-time fade test (less fade makes run 19 worse) and run 33 (forcing a slower fade breaks the readout), this makes three results saying the same thing: on this task, with this network, a fading count is the solution training prefers, not a trap it fell into.

run38.title: Erase bias shift −1
run38.lesson: Killed at 300, the same shape as run 33: running score 3.52 at 200, 4.21 at 300, frozen check 4.18 and worsening. Exam at the 300 checkpoint: 3.07 with F, 5.91 without; erase at food 0.239, away 0.0030. Measured. Half the shift of run 33 gave half the damage and the same direction: the readout does not re-match to a slower fade within the budget, and the wipe at food drops with the shift.

run39.title: Erase bias shift −0.5
run39.lesson: 1.57 at 30 s, the reset intact (0.33 at food) and the fade lowered a little (0.0062 from 0.0077). Inside the recipe's noise on its own, but the first fade shift that did not hurt, which makes it a candidate for a ratchet. Memory in F (5.92 without), erase at food 0.327, away 0.0062, write follows speed +0.76, 32 compass cells.

run40.title: Run 28's recipe (F-size penalty), seed 1
run40.lesson: 1.59 at 30 s. With run 28 (1.60) and run 41 (1.49) the penalty recipe has three draws: mean 1.56, spread 0.06, against the plain recipe's 1.72 over five seeds. Memory in F (5.92 without), erase at food 0.307, away 0.0065, write follows speed +0.72, 31 compass cells.

run41.title: Run 28's recipe (F-size penalty), seed 2
run41.lesson: 1.49 at 30 s with 38% arriving: the lowest exam score of both campaigns. Third draw of the penalty recipe (1.60, 1.59, 1.49). Memory in F (5.92 without), erase at food 0.36, away 0.007, write follows speed +0.70, 33 compass cells.

run44.title: Stack (F penalty + shift −0.5) from run 41, seed 2
run44.lesson: Collapsed: running score 6.00 at 200 and 5.63 at 300, frozen check 5.76; killed. Exam at the 300 checkpoint: 4.12 with F, 5.79 without. Measured. One of three draws of the stack failed outright while the other two trained normally, which says the half-unit shift on run 41 sits at the edge of what its readout can absorb: some training dice carry it over, some do not.

run42.title: Stack (F penalty + shift −0.5) from run 41, seed 0
run42.lesson: 1.66 at 30 s from run 41's 1.49. The half-unit shift lowered the fade to 0.0046 and the wipe at food to 0.21, and the score went up, not down. Memory in F, erase at food 0.21, away 0.0046, write follows speed +0.75, 30 compass cells.

run43.title: Stack (F penalty + shift −0.5) from run 41, seed 1
run43.lesson: 1.64 at 30 s from run 41's 1.49. Same picture as run 42: fade 0.0044, wipe at food 0.21, score worse than the parent. Memory in F, erase at food 0.208, away 0.0044, write follows speed +0.71, 34 compass cells.

run45.title: Run 28's recipe (F-size penalty), seed 3
run45.lesson: 1.55 at 30 s and 1.40 at 20 s. Fourth draw of the penalty recipe: 1.60, 1.59, 1.49, 1.55; mean 1.56, spread 0.05, against the plain recipe's 1.72 over five draws. Memory in F, erase at food 0.389, away 0.0098, write follows speed +0.64, 37 compass cells.
